content: 1. Sodium sulfate, sodium bicarbonate, sodium chloride, and potassium chloride powder for solution should be prepared by mixing 240 mL (8 oz) of the powder with water. The solution should be consumed orally every 10 minutes until a total of 4 liters is consumed or until the rectal effluent becomes clear. Rapid consumption of each portion is preferred over continuous sipping of small amounts. 2. For nasogastric (NG) administration, the solution should be delivered at a rate of 20-30 mL per minute until 4 liters are administered or until the rectal effluent is clear. 3. Oral powder should be prepared by dissolving 17 grams (approximately one heaping spoonful) in 240 mL (8 oz) of clear liquid. This should be consumed every 10 minutes until a total of 2,000 mL is consumed. Administration should begin within 6 hours after taking bisacodyl delayed-release tablets or magnesium citrate. 4. For maintenance use, 17 grams of oral powder (approximately one heaping spoonful) should be dissolved in 120-240 mL (4-8 oz) of a beverage and taken once daily. This should not be used for more than 1-2 weeks unless directed by a healthcare professional. 5. The safety and efficacy of sodium bicarbonate, sodium chloride, and potassium chloride have not been established in patients under 6 months of age or in neonates. 6. Common gastrointestinal side effects include abdominal bloating, cramping, and distension. Other potential adverse effects include colonic mucosal aphthous ulcerations, diarrhea, flatulence, ischemic colitis, and nausea. 7. Cardiovascular side effects may include arrhythmias, atrial fibrillation, peripheral edema, asystole, and acute pulmonary edema following aspiration. 8. Neurological side effects may include tremors and seizures. 9. Hypersensitivity reactions may manifest as urticaria, rash, pruritus, dermatitis, rhinorrhea, dyspnea, chest and throat tightness, fever, angioedema, anaphylaxis, and anaphylactic shock. 10. Gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as nausea, abdominal fullness, and bloating are common, occurring in up to 50% of patients. Less common reactions include abdominal cramps, vomiting, anal irritation, upper gastrointestinal bleeding (e.g., Mallory-Weiss tear), esophageal perforation (often associated with GERD), ileus, gastrointestinal obstruction, gastric retention, toxic colitis, bowel perforation, and toxic megacolon. 11. Osmotic laxative products may cause colonic mucosal aphthous ulcerations, with reports of more severe cases of ischemic colitis requiring hospitalization. Concomitant use of stimulant laxatives may increase the risk of ischemic colitis and is not recommended. 12. Generalized tonic-clonic seizures and/or loss of consciousness have been reported in patients without a prior history of seizures. These events resolved with correction of fluid and electrolyte abnormalities. Caution is advised in patients with a history of seizures or those at increased risk, including those taking medications that lower the seizure threshold, withdrawing from alcohol or benzodiazepines, or with suspected hyponatremia or low serum osmolality. 13. Patients with impaired gag reflex, swallowing abnormalities, or those prone to regurgitation or aspiration should be closely observed during administration, especially if the solution is administered via a nasogastric tube. 14. Use is contraindicated in patients with bowel obstruction, megacolon, perforated bowel, ulcerative colitis, toxic colitis, or gastric retention. 15. This product is not indicated for children under 2 years of age due to the risk of hypoglycemia, dehydration, and hypokalemia. 16. When using polyethylene glycol (PEG) as a laxative, it should not be used for more than one week. Prolonged use may lead to electrolyte imbalances, which can result in arrhythmias, seizures, and renal impairment. 17. Patients should maintain adequate hydration before, during, and after treatment. Post-colonoscopy laboratory tests may be considered if significant dehydration or vomiting occurs. 18. Caution is advised in patients at risk for cardiac arrhythmias, including those with unstable angina, congestive heart failure, recent myocardial infarction, uncontrolled arrhythmias, or cardiomyopathy. Preand post-dose ECG monitoring may be considered in these patients. 19. The product should not be combined with starch-based thickeners, as polyethylene glycol (PEG) can reduce the viscosity of starch-thickened liquids, potentially leading to choking and aspiration in patients with dysphagia. 20. Patients with renal impairment or those taking medications that may adversely affect renal function (e.g., ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs, diuretics, ARBs) should use this product with caution. Adequate hydration should be maintained, and preand post-dose laboratory tests (e.g., electrolytes, creatinine, BUN) may be considered. 21. Direct observation of administration is recommended for patients at risk of aspiration. 22. The product is not intended for direct ingestion and must be diluted with water before use. 23. Caution is advised in patients over 60 years of age, as serious adverse events have been reported in this population. 24. The product is classified as Pregnancy Category C. There is no data available regarding its use during lactation. 25. Patients should follow specific product instructions for bowel preparation as provided in the package or by their physician. Refrigerating the solution before administration may improve palatability. 26. Patients should fast for at least 3-4 hours before administering polyethylene glycol (PEG). Rapid consumption of each portion is encouraged. 27. For MiraLax, the bottle cap serves as a measuring cup marked to contain 17 grams. Patients should be instructed to hydrate adequately with water and/or clear liquids before, during, and after use.
